title: Risk and Position Sizing
summary: How to size trades, set stops, read expectancy and limit losses. Education only, not advice.

modules.title: Types of Trading Risk and Your Risk Budget
modules.subject: Risk types and budgets
modules.learned: Name the main types of trading risk and set a cash risk budget with a total open-risk limit.

check.q: A trader with a 5,000 USD account wants to risk no more than 2 percent on one trade. What should she do first?
options: Choose the trade and then decide how much to lose
Calculate the cash limit, 100 USD, and write it down before entering
Double the risk after a winning trade
check.explanation: Setting the cash limit first makes the loss decision before entry. Two percent of 5,000 USD is 100 USD.

modules.title: Position Sizing with a Fixed-Risk Rule
modules.subject: Position sizing
modules.learned: Calculate a position size from a fixed cash risk and a stop distance, and round it down to the allowed quantity.

check.q: A cash risk budget is 50 USD and the risk per unit is 0.50. The broker accepts whole units. What is the position size?
check.explanation: Fifty divided by 0.50 is 100 units. Whole units are accepted, so no rounding is needed here.

modules.title: Placing Stops That Match Your Trade Idea
modules.subject: Stops and invalidation
modules.learned: Place a stop beyond the invalidation level and explain how a change in stop distance changes the position size.

check.q: A trader widens her stop from 1 to 2 units below entry and keeps a fixed 100 USD risk. What should happen to her position size?
check.explanation: A wider stop means each unit carries more risk, so the size must fall to keep the same cash loss.

modules.title: Expectancy and Reward-to-Risk
modules.subject: Expectancy
modules.learned: Calculate expectancy and break-even win rate, and judge a method only after costs and on a large enough sample.

check.q: A method wins half of its trades. The average win is 100 USD and the average loss is 80 USD. What is the expectancy per trade before costs?
check.explanation: Half the trades win 100 and half lose 80, so the average is 50 minus 40, which is 10 USD per trade before costs.

modules.title: Drawdown, Recovery and Loss Limits
modules.subject: Drawdown
modules.learned: Measure drawdown from peak equity, calculate the gain needed to recover, and set loss limits in advance.

check.q: A trader reaches her daily loss limit early in the session. What should she do?
options: Keep trading with a bigger size to recover
Stop new trades for the day and record what happened
Move the limit higher so she can keep trading
Switch to a market she has never traded
check.explanation: A daily limit is a stop rule. Recording the day lets the review decide the next step, not a bigger trade.

modules.title: Leverage, Margin and Your Written Risk Plan
modules.subject: Leverage and risk plan
modules.learned: Calculate the leverage ratio of a position, explain margin calls, and write a one-page risk plan.

check.q: A trader holds a 4,000 USD position with 1,000 USD of equity. Price moves 5 percent against her. What is the loss?
check.explanation: Five percent of the 4,000 USD position is 200 USD, which is 20 percent of the 1,000 USD equity.

questions.q: A trader has a 10,000 USD account and a 1.5 percent risk budget. What is the cash limit for one trade?
She holds three open positions, each risking 100 USD. Her total open-risk limit is 250 USD. A fourth setup would also risk 100 USD. What should she do?
options: Open it, because each trade risks only 100 USD
Skip it, because total open risk would reach 400 USD, above the limit
Open it and close one position later
Raise the limit so the trade fits

questions.q: A trader's stop is 2 units below entry, but a weekend gap opens the price 6 units lower. Which risk has affected the exit?
Why should a trader write down the maximum loss before entering a trade?
options: Because prices always move in the expected direction
Because a written figure is needed to place an order
Because the risk budget changes each week
Because decisions made during a trade tend to reflect fear or hope

questions.q: Her account equity is 6,000 USD, including 200 USD of open profit. What is the cash amount of a 2 percent risk budget?
A trader has a 60 USD risk budget and the risk per unit is 0.75. What is the position size?
The budget is 50 USD, the risk per unit is 0.80, and the broker accepts whole units only. What size should she use?
A trader buys 62 units at 25.00 and her stop limits the loss to 49.60 USD. Which statement is true?
options: Position value and risk are the same
Position value is 49.60 USD and the risk is 1,550 USD
Position value is 1,550 USD and the loss if the stop works is 49.60 USD
The loss is 1,550 USD if the stop works

questions.q: After two strong weeks, a trader wants to double her size. Her plan sets a fixed 1 percent per trade. What should she do?
options: Double the size, because the method has worked
Halve the size to protect the gains
Keep 1 percent, letting the cash budget grow with equity
Round the size up to the next lot

questions.q: Her calculated size is 118.6 units. What should she do?
options: Use the position value as the size
Round down to 118 units, the largest whole size within budget

questions.q: A trader buys because price holds above a support area near 11.90. Where is the invalidation level?
options: Below the support area, where a clean break would prove the reason wrong
Far above the entry, at the previous high
Anywhere within 1 percent of the entry

questions.q: With a fixed 120 USD risk, the stop moves from 1.50 to 3.00 below entry, and the size stays at 80 units. What is the new risk?
A stop order sits 0.50 below entry. A weekend gap opens the price 1.00 below entry. What is the likely fill?
options: At the first price available, about 1.00 below entry

questions.q: A trader moves a losing trade's stop further from the price to avoid being stopped out. What is the problem?
options: It is correct, because stops should always be wide
It raises the planned loss after entry, which breaks the plan
It has no effect on the risk
It removes the need for a broker

questions.q: A trader wants an exit to trigger once price reaches a level, even if the fill is worse than the level. Which order fits?
options: A market order placed in the evening

questions.q: A method wins 40 percent of trades. The average win is 150 USD and the average loss is 100 USD. What is the expectancy per trade?
A method has a reward-to-risk ratio of 3. What is its break-even win rate before costs?
A method has an expectancy of 5 USD per trade before costs, and costs are 5 USD per trade. What is the real expectancy?
After 20 demo trades a trader sees a positive expectancy. What is the most careful conclusion?
options: The sample is small, so keep recording before judging
The method should be doubled in size

questions.q: A method has a reward-to-risk ratio of 2. At what win rate does it break even before costs?
An account falls from 5,000 USD to 4,000 USD. What is the drawdown?
What gain is needed to recover a 20 percent loss?
A trader reaches her daily loss limit. Which response follows a drawdown plan?
options: Trade smaller until the loss is recovered
Stop new trades for the period, then review the record
Double the size on the next trade
Trade a different market to recover faster

questions.q: What gain is needed to recover a 30 percent loss?
A trader's results show she is trading larger after each loss to win the money back. What is this called?
options: Trading a method that has worked before
Closing positions at the end of the day
Revenge trading, which means trading to win back a loss with larger size and less care

questions.q: A trader holds a 6,000 USD position on 2,000 USD of equity. What is the leverage ratio?
Her account equity is 1,000 USD and she holds a 10,000 USD position. Price falls 10 percent. What is the loss?
Why is a margin call dangerous?
options: It is only a warning with no effect
It can close positions after the price has already moved against you

questions.q: A trader considers adding funds to a losing leveraged position to avoid a margin call. What should she check first?
options: Whether the price will recover tomorrow
Whether the written plan's limits and actions allow it
How many friends trade the same market
How large the advertised return is

questions.q: Which item belongs in a one-page risk plan?
options: Per-trade risk, loss limits, a leverage cap and a review schedule
A list of social media tips
